clue.text: Twice as expensive? Oh, my!

indicators.note: twice says the word for expensive is written two times in a row

parts.note: dear means costly or expensive

explanation.surface: Someone gasps at a price that has doubled.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled word is an old-fashioned exclamation of dismay, much like saying goodness me.

clue.text: Representation in holding company

indicators.note: holding means the word in grips the company abbreviation inside it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A stake in a holding company described in business terms.
explanation.definitionFit: An image or symbol standing for something is a representation of it, as in a religious picture or screen symbol.

clue.text: Hired hands?

parts.note: reads as farm labourers, but means people paid to clap their hands in a theatre audience

explanation.definitionFit: A group paid to applaud a performer is exactly a band of hired clapping hands.

clue.text: Fugitive takes cover in English diocese

indicators.note: takes means the diocese word swallows the cover word inside it

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
a cap is a head covering

explanation.surface: A runaway hides out within an English bishop's territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has escaped from custody is a fugitive on the run.

clue.text: On the way to secure the first course baked in pastry

indicators.note: to secure means the phrase for on the way holds a letter tight inside it

parts.note: en route is French borrowed into English for on the way

indicators.note: the first picks just the opening letter of course

explanation.surface: A diner on the way to a restaurant is promised a pastry-baked starter.
explanation.definitionFit: The French culinary phrase describes food cooked in a pastry crust.

clue.text: Study before exam with a National Trust rival

indicators.note: before places the study word ahead of the exam word

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
a test is an exam
NT is the abbreviation for the National Trust, a British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A student cramming for an exam alongside a National Trust competitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor in a contest is someone's rival for the prize.

clue.text: Began vigorous action, being captured by the enemy

definitions.meaning: to set about something with energy, as when diners attack their food
a town that is taken by the enemy is said to have been lost to them in battle

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to start eagerly and to be conquered by an attacker.

clue.text: Labour candidate — he's accepted dirty money that must be returned

indicators.note: accepted means the letters of he's take in another piece inside them

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

indicators.note: must be returned means the word for dirty money is read backwards

parts.note: filthy lucre is ill-gotten money

explanation.surface: A Labour Party candidate taking bribes that must be paid back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks political but refers to the Twelve Labours of the Greek hero; 'must be returned' turns LUCRE into ERCUL.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical strongman was set twelve labours, so he is a fitting candidate for any labour.

clue.text: Loop lines quickly turn east then south

indicators.note: turn means the word for quickly is reversed

parts.note: soon means quickly, before long
E is the compass abbreviation for east
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Directions for a train on a loop line turning east then south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loop lines' suggests railway branch lines, but here means loops tied in ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: Each is a loop made in a line of rope that tightens when pulled, so they are loop lines.

clue.text: Club used in the evening

definitions.meaning: a golf club with a metal head
a household appliance employed for evening out creases in clothes

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a golf club and the appliance that smooths fabric flat.

clue.text: After the game, Scrabble piece found on the floor

parts.note: quarry is game, the animal being hunted
the letters in Scrabble are on small tiles

explanation.surface: After a board game, a Scrabble tile turns up on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like the board game but is hunted prey.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of hard unglazed tile is used for flooring, so it is found on the floor.

clue.text: He should honour his agreement to the letter

definitions.text: He should honour his agreement to the letter

parts.words: He should honour his agreement to the letter
parts.note: seems to praise someone exact in keeping promises, but describes a tenant bound by a lease to the person who lets property

explanation.definitionFit: A tenant holding a lease owes duties under that agreement to the landlord who let it.

clue.text: Almost sure to take a turn in the air

indicators.note: to take, in the sense of take a different shape, signals that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something nearly certain to change direction while airborne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' suggests dropping a letter from sure, but both words are the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobatic flip in which the body rolls head over heels in the air.

clue.text: One slum I refurbish — with this?

definitions.text: One slum I refurbish — with this?

indicators.note: refurbish means to make over, so these letters are made over into a new order

explanation.surface: A landlord planning to do up a slum wonders what to paint it with.
explanation.definitionFit: A type of water-based paint used on walls when redecorating a home.

clue.text: It takes travellers by road and rail

definitions.text: It takes travellers by road and rail

parts.words: It takes travellers by road and rail
parts.note: a vehicle running on rails laid along a road, carrying passengers

explanation.definitionFit: A street tram runs on rails set into the road, carrying passengers.

clue.text: Everyone present and alert

definitions.meaning: the phrase said at roll call when nobody is missing
mentally sharp, with all one's wits about one

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both that the whole group has turned up and that someone is quick-witted.

clue.text: Looks kind, often

definitions.meaning: gazes or considers, as a verb
the word often follows kind in a letter's sign-off, meaning good wishes

explanation.definitionFit: The word means gazes at, and also the good wishes closing a letter, as in kind ones.

clue.text: Game that may leave one cold

definitions.meaning: a board game played with round counters
currents of chilly air through a room

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a board game and also chilly air currents that make a person cold.

clue.text: Foreign money invested in source of sugar and spice

indicators.note: invested in means the money is placed inside another word

parts.note: sugar cane is a source of sugar
the yen is the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: Overseas capital is put into the sugar and spice trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot red pepper powder used as a spice in cooking.

clue.text: It sounds a beastly form of warfare

indicators.note: it sounds says the word that follows is heard, not seen

parts.note: a gorilla is a large beast, an ape

explanation.surface: A remark that a kind of fighting is brutal and animal-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Irregular fighting by small independent bands is a form of warfare.

clue.text: Goes through customs at university

parts.note: uses are customs or habitual practices
up means in residence at a university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Someone passes through customs while at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To go through a supply is to consume it entirely.

clue.text: Take a chance with a fish shop

parts.note: to bet is to gamble or take a chance
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.walkthrough: 'shop' looks like a noun but is the verb meaning to inform on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is slang for informing on them, which is to betray them.

clue.text: It may be pressed down, but not up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the word not is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written before turning

explanation.surface: A remark that something can be pushed down but never up.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch or key that you push to operate a device.

clue.text: Indifference to detail

definitions.meaning: aloofness or lack of emotional involvement
in military use, a small group of troops detailed for a special task

explanation.definitionFit: The word means emotional distance and also a unit of soldiers sent on a separate duty.

clue.text: Drunk in the centre of Oxford?

definitions.meaning: the main street of central Oxford is known simply as the ...

explanation.definitionFit: The word means intoxicated and also names Oxford's main street, the High.

clue.text: Exclamation of surprise when doubled up in laughter

indicators.note: doubled up means the short exclamation is written twice

parts.note: ha is a cry of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone cries out in surprise while bent double with mirth.
explanation.definitionFit: The repeated syllable represents the sound of someone laughing.

clue.text: The calls he makes are always noted

definitions.text: The calls he makes are always noted

parts.words: The calls he makes are always noted
parts.note: seems to be about someone whose phone calls are logged, but means a military musician whose calls are musical notes

explanation.definitionFit: A soldier sounding reveille or the last post plays calls made of musical notes.

clue.text: The Pony Express's first new recruit

indicators.note: new means the letters appear in a new arrangement
first takes just the opening letter of Express's

explanation.surface: The Pony Express takes on its first fresh rider.
explanation.definitionFit: A beginner or newcomer to a group is a recent recruit.
